question: It was decided to celebrate the Republic day on 26th January every year by the Constitution makers to pay homage to the ‘Purna Swaraj’ declaration which was promulgated on _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**26th January 1930**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The decision to celebrate Republic Day on 26th January was to mark the anniversary of the 'Purna Swaraj' declaration.
 
• The 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) declaration was made on 26th January 1930 by the Indian National Congress.
 
• On this day in 1930, the Indian National Congress proclaimed the Declaration of Independence from British rule.
 
• Celebrating Republic Day on this date was intended to honor the significant event in India's struggle for independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Purna Swaraj**

 
 
• The term 'Purna Swaraj' translates to 'Complete Independence'.
 
• It was a resolution passed by the Indian National Congress in the Lahore session in December 1929.
 
• The resolution marked the Congress's call for complete self-rule, free from British control.
 
• On 26th January 1930, the Congress declared it as 'Independence Day', urging Indians to aspire for complete independence.
 
 
 
• **Republic Day**
 
 
• Republic Day is celebrated on 26th January every year in India.
 
• It commemorates the day when the Constitution of India came into effect in 1950, making India a sovereign, democratic republic.
 
• The day is marked by grand celebrations, including a parade in the capital, New Delhi, showcasing India's cultural diversity and military strength.
 
• It is a national holiday in India, reflecting the significance of the day in the country's history.
 
 
 
• **Indian National Congress**
 
 
• The Indian National Congress (INC) was founded in 1885.
 
• It played a pivotal role in the Indian independence movement against British rule.
 
• The INC was instrumental in mobilizing the Indian population and organizing protests, civil disobedience movements, and negotiations with the British government.
 
• Many prominent leaders like Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Subhas Chandra Bose were associated with the INC.
